purpose: Determine whether the many-to-one segmentation topology found by PHOST-PF1A predicts target recovery and photometric residuals after magnitude and local background are controlled.
frozenInputs: The 142 author identities and the 284-row PHOST-PF1A ledger
The even-ID development and odd-ID validation split
The 32 relevant NIRCam module-B calibrated exposures: four dithers times four short-wave detectors in each of F090W and F150W
Collision strata defined by center-label state, label multiplicity, isophotal area, centroid distance, local background, period, magnitude, colour, and component before injection outcomes

pilot.sample: Forty-eight sealed target environments balanced across blank, isolated-label, and large-collision states and across spiral and tidal components where support exists.
pilot.intervention: At each environment inject one star at a time at preregistered nearby offsets that preserve detector, label topology, and background while avoiding the real target core. Use 64 magnitude-colour draws per environment for 3,072 injections per band and pipeline.
pilot.referencePipeline: DOLPHOT NIRCam with versioned PSF files, masks, sky products, alignment logs, and a frozen parameter file following the published JWST workflow.
pilot.independentPipeline: A separately implemented fixed-scene PSF or linear field-deblending model that shares only the input exposure manifest and injection list.
pilot.outputs: One row per injection including non-detections, input and output flux, crowding, sharpness, fit flags, collision stratum, and pipeline identity.

hypotheses.claim: Collision topology adds no information once magnitude and local background are matched.
hypotheses.prediction: Within matched cells, inclusion and median residual differ by less than 0.02 and 0.01 mag across collision states.
hypotheses.reject: A simultaneous interval excludes both tolerances in the same direction in both pipelines.

hypotheses.claim: The apparent component recoverability difference is mediated by collision topology rather than component identity itself.
hypotheses.prediction: Conditioning on collision and background removes the component coefficient while preserving calibrated injection coverage.
hypotheses.reject: A component coefficient remains and predicts held-out odd-ID inclusion in both pipelines.

hypotheses.claim: Exposure-level PSF residuals can bridge catalog misses to target-specific magnitudes.
hypotheses.prediction: Injected and real-source residual diagnostics share support and both pipelines agree within 0.01 mag over supported strata.
hypotheses.reject: Real residuals lie outside injection support or pipelines disagree beyond 0.01 mag.

uncertaintyBudget.control: Version and hash PSFs; compare DOLPHOT with an independent scene model
Archive every mask and alignment log by exposure and freeze on even IDs
Simultaneous binomial and residual intervals by sealed cell
uncertaintyBudget.stop: Cells lack the precision to distinguish the registered effect

uncertaintyBudget.control: Compare injected and real PSF, background, sharpness, and residual distributions
Keep phase uncertainty separate from measurement residuals
uncertaintyBudget.stop: Aperture residuals are interpreted as mean magnitudes

uncertaintyBudget.control: Cluster uncertainty by exposure, detector, and calibration ancestor
uncertaintyBudget.stop: Object counts average common terms down

success: Both pipelines close the injection ledger, agree on inclusion within 0.02 and median residual within 0.01 mag over supported strata, and make a stable odd-ID branch decision without changing the target population.
failure: Pipeline disagreement, unsupported collision cells, phase-selection leakage, or residual mismatch blocks a component-distance interpretation but still localizes which bridge failed.
claimBoundary: Passing the pilot would validate or reject collision topology as a missingness mechanism over tested environments. It would not close the author phase-selection ledger, a second epoch, the full component covariance, or H0.
